title: Build an Operating System, Part 2
summary: Take your kernel from a single privileged program to a real multitasking system: ring 3, the syscall instruction, address spaces, preemption, locks, a filesystem and pipes.
description: Continue Part 1 with ring 3, the syscall instruction, per-process page tables and timer-driven preemption. Then implement a physical frame bitmap, a small heap, wait queues, an interrupt-safe spinlock, a RAM disk and a pipe. Finish by reviewing independent file offsets. The sandbox boots your freestanding C under QEMU; several lessons inspect real processor state, while later exercises isolate kernel data structures.
outcomes: Add user mode, preemption, address spaces, files and pipes to a kernel.
